contracts.description: Cookies, signing, encryption, Fetch Metadata, authentication and old browser tabs
contracts.notes: Historical token-era Rails parity receipts remain baseline evidence for cookies and login. Current native tests verify token-free forms, HTTPS login/setup/transfers, metadata/origin/TLS rejection, trusted proxy context and signed owner-authorized disk uploads; Rails CSRF crypto vectors remain historical compatibility tests, not active browser protection.

contracts.description: Ordered recognition, URL generation, verbs, formats and nested params
contracts.notes: Pinned ordered route/verb recognition, optional/Accept formats, request/parameter failures, public documents and trusted local proxy URL context pass.

contracts.description: Schema, encodings, nullability, typecasting and bidirectional writes
contracts.notes: Pinned schema and scalar casts, complete mutation/FTS/storage snapshots, transactional failure boundaries, fresh schema bootstrap and bidirectional production rollback pass.

contracts.description: Callbacks, transactions, cancellation, outbox and post-commit effects
contracts.notes: Message/boost/room/user/account/attachment mutations, dirty tracking, injected rollback failures and post-commit queue/broadcast effects pass. Post-commit jobs go to the in-process queue (test/jobs_test.exs).

contracts.description: Templates, helper escaping, frontend assets and browser interactions
contracts.notes: Byte comparisons plus actual Chromium composer, file uploads, room/profile/account edits and logout pass. Rich-text comparison retains the documented escaping/error rules.

contracts.description: Existing keys, checksums, signatures, variants, ranges and downloads
contracts.notes: Existing signed uploads/downloads/ranges, replacements/purges/embeds, loader/saver/conversion image operations and image/video/audio/PDF bytes/state pass.

contracts.description: Claims, retry, schedules, shutdown, mail and external integrations
contracts.notes: Actual queue claims, failures/no retries, processed stats, worker drain, webhook replies/timeout/protocol boundaries and real isolated encrypted HTTPS push delivery pass. Resque is replaced by the in-process, non-durable Campfire.Worker, as in the Rust port: bounded per-class queues, per-class concurrency and drain on graceful shutdown (test/jobs_test.exs). The listed receipts were recorded with Redis and Resque.

contracts.description: Cable or polling, authorization, revocation and unique-user fanout
contracts.notes: Cable protocol/authorization, cross-runtime pubsub, message/boost/room/involvement fanout, session/ban/deactivation revocation and browser lifecycle pass. Broadcasts and disconnects are delivered in process (Campfire.CableFanout, test/cable_fanout_test.exs), as in the Rust port. cable-interop.json was recorded with the Redis bridge.

contracts.description: Environment, readiness, deployment, metrics and rollback rehearsal
contracts.notes: Native production release with pinned Thruster TLS/HTTP2, fresh first-run and real worker, ONCE backup/restore, in-flight HTTP/job drain and Rails→Elixir→Rails rollback pass on isolated volumes. The container runs no Redis or separate worker; jobs drain in process on shutdown, as in the Rust port. The listed rollback and in-flight job drain receipts were recorded with Redis and Resque, when Rails and Elixir could share a live install.

benchmark_status: complete: frozen candidate measured in four balanced rounds per build; clean native x86_64 run regressed, ARM64 shared-host observations failed the drained-job audit
